html:
The Baré are an Arawakan people of the upper Rio Negro in the Amazon, on the borders of Brazil and Venezuela, near the Casiquiare, the natural channel that links the Amazon to the Orinoco. They should not be confused with the Barí of the Colombian Andes, whose name is similar.

The Baré were a large river people, farmers and traders who travelled by canoe. In the 1700s Portuguese slave raids and missions on the Rio Negro hit them hard, and many were taken downriver. They shifted from their own Arawakan language to Nheengatu, the Tupi-based common language spread by the missions, and later to Portuguese and Spanish. Today several thousand Baré live around São Gabriel da Cachoeira in Brazil and in Venezuela.
